cohort: The study included 539 mothers who gave birth between September 2019 and August 2021 at Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital in Tigray, Ethiopia, categorized into exposed (with APH) and non-exposed (without APH) groups.
finding: Antepartum hemorrhage is associated with an increased risk of adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, including postpartum hemorrhage, emergency cesarean section, preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth, perinatal death, a low Apgar score, and admission to the NICU.
mod_finding: Mothers with antepartum hemorrhage were significantly more likely to experience an emergency cesarean section compared to those without APH (ARR = 2.9, 95% CI: 2.1, 3.9).
birth_weight: Low birth weight baby was an outcome measured.
gest_age: Preterm birth was an outcome measured.
